title: BirdMoE: Reducing Communication Costs for Mixture-of-Experts Training Using Load-Aware Bi-random Quantization
problem: MoE model parallelism in LLM training (e.g., ChatGPT) faces intensive all-to-all collective communication of intermediate results between expert nodes, substantially degrading training efficiency.
motivation: MoE architectures enable efficient scaling of LLM training but introduce all-to-all communication bottleneck between expert nodes that becomes the critical efficiency limiter.
method: BirdMoE reduces communication overhead during training by using bi-random quantization: it randomly converts floating-point numbers (decimals used in computations) to integers while keeping the mathematical average the same, so training quality is preserved despite using fewer bits. It then applies a mixed-precision strategy, meaning it dynamically adjusts how much compression each expert node uses based on how busy it is, which balances the all-to-all communication load (where every expert node sends results to every other expert node).
key_novelty: The core idea is load-aware bi-random quantization—a technique that randomly converts data to smaller representations while mathematically preserving accuracy—enabling expert nodes to dynamically adjust compression based on how busy they are.
contributions: Random Quantization with expectation invariance for lossless integer mapping
Load-aware Mixed Precision strategy for dynamic load balancing
Communication compression technique preserving MoE training quality
baselines: SOTA compression techniques for MoE training
limitations: Not discussed; focus is on compression and load balancing.
primary_theme: Load-aware quantization for MoE collective communication compression
